works.title: Flamenco Vivo (Canciones Populares Antiguas) [Recopiladas por Federico García Lorca]

position_in_era.primary_genre_lineage: cante hondo × Lorca poetic recovery (deep traditional cante on traditional repertoire)
position_in_era.historical_role: Cited as one of the leading exponents of cante hondo of the second half of the 20th century. *Flamenco Vivo* (1996) is her interpretation of the popular songs collected and harmonised by Federico García Lorca in 1931 — a recovery of the deep Andalusian song tradition that flamenco arose from. Princess of Asturias Prize for Arts (2022). User has 'Zorongo Gitano' from this album in red-heart (2026-02-10) — a closing signal that the listener's ear has gone deep into the cante root that Dorantes' translation aesthetic flows out of.

narrative_slots.production_facts: Released 1996. The repertoire is Lorca's transcriptions of *canciones populares antiguas* (1931).
narrative_slots.member_dynamics: Born 1951 in Linares (Jaén); generational peer of Paco de Lucía, Camarón, Enrique Morente, José Mercé, Manolo Sanlúcar, Tomatito.
narrative_slots.cultural_venue: Madrid mature-cante circuit; international concert halls.
narrative_slots.instrumentation_details: Cante with flamenco guitar; on this album frequent palmas and minimal percussion.
narrative_slots.release_circumstances: Premio Nacional de Música 2001; Princess of Asturias Award 2022.
